self.description: Series containing only non-null string elements
Series containing string elements mixed with NaN (np.nan or None)
self.constraints: st.builds(pd.Series, st.lists(st.one_of(st.text(min_size=0, max_size=20), st.none()), min_size=2, max_size=10)).filter(lambda s: s.isna().any())

pat.description: Character sequence without regex special characters
Valid regular expression with metacharacters such as \d, .*, \w+

flags.description: Flags to pass through to the re module, e.g. re.IGNORECASE

na.description: Fill value for missing values set to False
Fill value for missing values set to True

regex.description: If True, assumes the pat is a regular expression
If False, treats the pat as a literal string

post_condition.source: Return boolean Series or Index based on whether a given pattern or regex is contained within a string of a Series or Index.
Returning a Series of booleans using only a literal pattern. >>> s1.str.contains('og', regex=False)
post_condition.expected_behavior: assert all(result.iloc[i] == (pat in self.iloc[i]) for i in range(len(self)))

post_condition.source: If True, assumes the pat is a regular expression.
post_condition.expected_behavior: assert all(result.iloc[i] == bool(re.search(pat, self.iloc[i])) for i in range(len(self)))

post_condition.source: Returning 'house' or 'dog' when either expression occurs in a string. >>> s1.str.contains('house|dog', regex=True)
post_condition.expected_behavior: assert all(result.iloc[i] == bool(re.search(pat, self.iloc[i])) for i in range(len(self)))
assert all(result.iloc[i] == (pat.lower() in self.iloc[i].lower()) for i in range(len(self)))

post_condition.source: Ignoring case sensitivity using flags with regex. >>> s1.str.contains('PARROT', flags=re.IGNORECASE, regex=True)
post_condition.expected_behavior: assert all(result.iloc[i] == bool(re.search(pat, self.iloc[i], re.IGNORECASE)) for i in range(len(self)))
assert all(result.iloc[i] == na for i in range(len(self)) if pd.isna(self.iloc[i]))

post_condition.source: Ensure pat is a not a literal pattern when regex is set to True. However, '.0' as a regex matches any character followed by a 0.
post_condition.expected_behavior: assert all(result.iloc[i] == (pat in self.iloc[i]) for i in range(len(self)))
